description:
The workload verdict compares defk with the optimized Elixir baseline; the comparison with a hand-written NIF is reported beside it (CONTEXT.md, "workload verdict"). Write the NIF a careful Elixir developer would write today: a Rustler crate with the same per-chunk aggregate function (hash map from the std library or ahash, the same parse), called the same way from the same Elixir chunking code, both as a DirtyCpu NIF and as a plain NIF (to show the scheduler gap the way examples/fuzzy_search does with search_blocking). Record build toolchain requirements beside defk's (Rust toolchain vs cc).

Also run a responsiveness probe during the full-size run: a 1 ms ticker as in bench/tick_gap.exs, reported for Elixir, defk and both NIF variants.

Done when: the NIF produces the same output as the baseline for two seeds, the three implementations are measured by the same harness, and the tick-gap numbers are recorded.
title: 1BRC: Rustler reference implementation for the native comparison
